html:
A grandson of Genghis Khan who became Great Khan of the Mongols in 1260 and founded the Yuan dynasty of China in 1271. In 1279 he completed the conquest of the Song, and became the first ruler not of Han Chinese birth to hold all of China.

He was a son of Tolui and his wife Sorghaghtani Beki. When his brother Mongke, the Great Khan, died in 1259, Kublai claimed the title. His younger brother Ariq Boke claimed it too, and they fought a civil war until 1264. Kublai won, but the Mongol Empire split for good. The khans of Persia, Central Asia and the Golden Horde went their own ways, and Kublai's real power was in China and Mongolia.

He ruled China in the Chinese style:

  • He took a Chinese dynastic name, Great Yuan, and built a new capital, Khanbaliq, on the site of modern Beijing.
  • He used Chinese advisers but gave top posts to Mongols and Central Asians.
  • He extended the Grand Canal to his capital and made paper money the main currency.

He was open to foreigners, and the Venetian Marco Polo claimed to have served him.

He also kept up the Mongol drive to expand. He sent fleets against Japan in 1274 and 1281, both wrecked in the Mongol invasions of Japan, and against Vietnam, Burma and Java, with little lasting gain. He died in 1294, and the Yuan lasted until 1368.
